source.title: Probing Knowledge Recovery in Unlearned Models

record.tranche_reason: It behaviorally tests whether ablating an extracted refusal direction changes refusal, but the text does not state enough about direction extraction or ablation to establish that it reproduces the original method exactly.
record.gate_note: Probe 1 reports refusal outcomes after refusal-direction ablation and a WMDP-Bio outcome for the one checkpoint with a clean direction. Probe 2's representation-targeted ablations and Probe 3's unrelated fine-tuning are different recovery interventions, so their results are not rows for the refusal-direction versions. The article does not report adding a refusal direction.
record.test_reason: The study uses refusal-direction ablation mainly as a tool for knowledge recovery. It does report refusal rates after ablation on held-out AdvBench prompts in a new setting (WMDP-unlearned Llama-3-8B-Instruct checkpoints). ILU-RMU fell from 98% to 0%; RMU fell only partially. These results bear on V1's ablation-removes-refusal part. Extraction details are not given, so exact T1 replication cannot be confirmed.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. For ILU-RMU, the only checkpoint with a clean refusal direction, ablation removed refusal but recovered no WMDP-Bio knowledge. The author infers that refusal is not the main suppression mechanism there. Representation-targeted ablation and unrelated SFT did recover benchmark accuracy in several checkpoints.
record.recipe_differences: The study extracts and ablates a refusal direction and validates its effect on held-out harmful prompts, but does not describe the direction-construction or ablation details needed to verify an exact match to the original method. The experiment focuses on WMDP-Bio recovery in unlearned checkpoints.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome depended on the checkpoint and its condition: only ILU-RMU yielded a clean refusal direction; RMU showed a partial reduction, while other checkpoints had absent refusal behavior or degeneration that prevented meaningful measurement.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-direction ablation in ILU-RMU did not recover WMDP-Bio accuracy: the CI excluded gains above 1.4 points. Matched and random control ablations were also null.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing the refusal direction does not restore knowledge suppressed by unlearning (ILU-RMU).

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning itself reduced refusal. IDK-AP refused 0% of AdvBench prompts vs 98% for base Llama, and RMU was also lower.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some unlearning methods degrade refusal behavior as a side effect.

record.problems: Only six Llama-3-8B-Instruct unlearned checkpoints were studied. A clean refusal direction was obtained for only one checkpoint; several others had absent refusal behavior or degeneration that prevented meaningful measurement. The text does not give the direction-extraction and ablation details needed to verify an exact reproduction. General capability preservation was not measured for the refusal-direction ablation.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out from the refusal-direction results. Results from the representation-targeted ablation and unrelated GSM8K fine-tuning probes were not cataloged as they use different interventions and do not test the listed refusal-direction versions.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal. Preservation of general capabilities (MMLU) after refusal-direction ablation. Whether the direction was difference-in-means over harmful vs harmless prompts, and the layer/position coverage of the ablation.
The unlearning methods vary, but there is no test of refusal training.

record.verdict_notes: This is a blog post (BlueDot sprint) and not peer reviewed. The V1 evidence is limited to one clean checkpoint and one partial one, with no numbers for RMU. Other checkpoints were uninterpretable because of degeneration or absent refusal, which may reflect the unlearning rather than any limit of V1.

versions.untested_parts: Direction addition and induced refusal on harmless requests were not tested. The text does not specify whether the tested direction was the harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction or whether ablation covered every layer and position. General capability preservation was not measured for the refusal-direction ablation.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration test.
No test of attacks suppressing the refusal direction or training against its ablation.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine subspace, cone, or multiple directions.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
The checkpoints use different unlearning methods, but the study does not test how or when refusal training creates a removable direction.

relation.reason: The post validates the refusal direction behaviourally per checkpoint and reports its ablation effect on refusal.

tranche.reason: New setting (WMDP-unlearned Llama-3-8B-Instruct checkpoints) with reported refusal rates after direction ablation on held-out AdvBench prompts: ILU-RMU 98% to 0%, RMU partial. This is a result on V1, not just use as a tool, and is not the original method replicated in detail.

source_check.notes: The pack listed verdicts with no [lN] ids, so l1 and l2 were assigned in listed order. The post does not give the direction-construction method, layer, prompt counts or refusal judge, and gives no uncertainty on refusal rates. IDK-AP is described as complying with 'most' harmful prompts yet having a 0% refusal rate.

statements.correction: ILU-RMU Llama-3-8B-Instruct: ablation cut held-out AdvBench refusal 98% to 0%. No addition/induction tested. No capability measure or uncertainty reported for the refusal-rate result itself. RMU direction only partially reduced refusal. IDK-AP had 0% refusal before ablation. GradDiff, NPO and NPO-ILU too degenerate to read. Clean direction in 1 of 6 checkpoints.
statements.problem: 98%->0% on held-out AdvBench for ILU-RMU is right. But this study tests removal only, not induction. Its capability and uncertainty flags come from other probes (MMLU in Probes 2/3, a CI on WMDP-Bio), not from the cited refusal result.
